activities.topic: Introduction to 3D Objects and Layer-Based Construction

activity_1.title: Find 3D Objects Around You
steps: Look around your house and find five objects that have length, width, and height.
Hold each object and observe its shape from different sides.

activity_2.title: Compare 2D and 3D
steps: Find two flat objects and two solid objects.
Observe the difference between flat (2D-like) and solid (3D) objects.
Notice how 3D objects have thickness and can be held, while flat objects cannot.
examples: Flat objects: page of a notebook, newspaper, wall calendar

activity_3.title: Create a Shape Using Layers
steps: Take small objects like coins, leaves, or papers.
Place them one above another to create a stack.
Observe how stacking layer by layer increases height.
Relate this to how 3D printers build objects layer by layer.

extra_exploration.task: Look around your home or village and find one broken object.

think_and_notice: Which object you found had the most interesting shape?
How does stacking layers increase the height of an object?
Why could 3D printing be useful in villages or homes?
activities.discussion_instruction: Discuss your ideas with your parents or elders.

learning_outcomes.title: Understand 3D shapes
learning_outcomes.description: Students recognize objects with length, width, and height.

learning_outcomes.title: Understand the layer-by-layer concept
learning_outcomes.description: Students observe how stacking layers builds a structure.

learning_outcomes.title: Develop observation and spatial reasoning skills
learning_outcomes.description: Students analyze shapes and structures around them.

learning_outcomes.title: Connect technology with real-life problem solving
learning_outcomes.description: Students imagine how 3D printing could help repair or create objects.

bonus_activity: Find three objects that could be designed on a computer and printed using a 3D printer.
Examples: keychain, small toy, bottle cap
Think about what new object you would like to design and print.

activities.topic: Machines as Systems of Connected Parts and Assembly

activity_1.title: Observe Machines Made of Parts
steps: Look around your house or village and find one machine made from many connected parts.
Observe the machine carefully and identify different parts that help it work.

activity_2.title: Try Simple Assembly
steps: Take 3–4 small objects from your home.
Stack or arrange them to build a small structure like a tower or bridge.
Observe how the structure becomes stronger when parts are arranged properly.

activity_3.title: Check Moving Parts
steps: Find an object that moves smoothly when pushed or rotated.
Observe how different parts help it move smoothly.

extra_exploration.task: Look around your home and find two objects that are fixed using bolts, screws, or nuts.

think_and_notice: Which machine had the most parts?
Why is it important that parts are fixed tightly in a machine?
What might happen if a machine is assembled incorrectly?
activities.discussion_instruction: Discuss your observations with your parents or elders.

learning_outcomes.title: Understand machines as systems of parts
learning_outcomes.description: Students observe how machines are built from multiple components.

learning_outcomes.title: Recognize the importance of proper assembly
learning_outcomes.description: Students understand that correct assembly ensures stability and smooth functioning.

learning_outcomes.title: Develop observation and analytical skills
learning_outcomes.description: Students analyze how different parts contribute to a machine's operation.

learning_outcomes.title: Connect engineering concepts with real life
learning_outcomes.description: Students relate everyday machines to how devices like 3D printers are assembled.

bonus_activity: Ask someone in your house which machine needs regular tightening or repair.
Examples: bicycle, farming tools, water pump
Think about why machines need maintenance to work properly.
